answer: Each agent must stake a scarce onyx token before it can submit jobs, and the protocol locks that stake until its work is checked against a randomly assigned verifier. A garden of independent verifiers can slash tokens for invalid results, while a vine of linked identities gains no extra influence because rewards are capped per stake, not per account. A sybil attacker must therefore buy more tokens and risk losing them on every fraudulent submission, making identities costly rather than free.
